newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei seen hovering near 18,000, eye on NCB.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei seen hovering near 18,000, eye on NCB.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key index is likely to hover just below the key 18,000 level on Thursday, as blue-chip issues that benefit from the weak yen will rise, while some leading exporters that have surged recently could see profit-taking, brokers said.
News that Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) and Bankers Trust are in the "final stages" of on a business tie-up will help NCB's shares, but the overall impact may be limited, they said.
On Wednesday, the 225-share Nikkei average finished 318.33 points or 1.77 percent lower at 17,703.37.
The Nikkei's June futures shed 330 points to close at 17,710.
"The NCB news will be good for its shares, but the Nikkei average's recovery is expected to be small," said Kenji Karikomi, deputy general manager at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.

Shares of leading exporters with bright earnings forecasts are likely to remain firmer, backed by the yen's weaker trend against the dollar, Karikome said, adding that some of them have risen too sharply and could be hit by corrective selling.
The dollar rose further overnight, trading at 127.05/15 yen in early Asia against 126.64/74 in late Tokyo on Wednesday.
